FACT: environment discrepancies recorded per AAP 0.10.7 — host OS observed as Ubuntu 25.10, and the curl and python3 versions in `_capture.tooling` differ from the 8.5.0 and 3.12.3 named in the instructions for this file. INFERENCE: neither difference affects an HTTPS GET capture; reasoning: the payloads are decoded JSON and no version-dependent behaviour of either tool is relied upon.

FACT: every record in `reviews`, `review_comments`, `issue_comments` and `pull_request` is verbatim as returned by the API — unpruned, unreordered, unformatted, with body text, user.login, author_association and all timestamps preserved character for character. No derived field was added inside any record. Records appear in API order and pages were concatenated in Link rel="next" order.

FACT: in_reply_to_id is preserved on inline review comments, and user.login and all timestamps are preserved on every record. INFERENCE: in_reply_to_id is what reconstructs the reply chain, and the identity fields are needed because later runs re-apply these third-party contributions with author attribution intact per AAP 0.10.5; reasoning: a flattened comment list loses the question-and-answer structure that makes a review thread adjudicable, and re-application creates new commits whose author can only come from this captured metadata.
FACT: distinct user.login values across the three families, echoed verbatim from the capture: ["Rune-Christensen", "samdion1994"].

FACT: review submission states echoed verbatim from the capture: {"CHANGES_REQUESTED": 1, "COMMENTED": 1}. Submissions carrying state == "CHANGES_REQUESTED": [{"id": 1694706276, "user_login": "Rune-Christensen", "submitted_at": "2023-10-24T12:30:27Z"}].

FACT: `_capture.record_counts` states the comparison the supplied ground truth invites, plainly and in one direction only: the phrase carried forward is “review comments”, the endpoint that returns review comments on a pull request is pulls/330/comments (`_capture.calls[2]`), the expected figure is 5 and the observed figure is 3. Locator: `aap_expected_review_comments_endpoint` names that endpoint, `actual_review_comments` holds 3, `expected_vs_actual_verdict` records CONTRADICTED and `corroborates_expected` is false. `endpoint_matching_expected_count` is retained as a separate, purely descriptive field: it names the family whose count happens to equal 5, which is the conversation family issues/330/comments (`_capture.calls[3]`). INFERENCE: it is not a corroboration and must not be read as one; reasoning: conversation comments are a different endpoint family from inline review comments, so counting one and reporting it against the other would substitute one endpoint for another, and they are not relabelled as one another here.

FACT: independent cross-check from the API itself — the captured `pull_request` payload carries review_comments = 3 and comments = 5, which agree exactly with the per-family record counts in `_capture.record_counts`. INFERENCE: the capture is therefore internally consistent with GitHub's own counters for this pull request; reasoning: those counters are computed server side and were returned by a different endpoint than the ones that produced the arrays, so agreement is an independent check rather than a restatement.

FACT: CONTRADICTION OF SUPPLIED GROUND TRUTH, stated explicitly per AAP 0.2.2 rather than reconciled — the ground truth records 5 review comments on pull request 330. The endpoint that returns review comments on a pull request is pulls/330/comments, and it returned 3. Expected 5, actual 3, contradicted. Locator: `_capture.record_counts.expected_vs_actual_verdict`. Two other captured counts also equal 5 and neither is offered as a substitute: the conversation endpoint issues/330/comments returned 5, and reviews (2) plus inline review comments (3) sums to 5. Both are recorded as arithmetic on the captured counts and nothing more. INFERENCE: neither establishes that the inline endpoint returned 5, and using either to declare the figure corroborated would substitute one endpoint family for another; reasoning: the two families are served by different URLs and GitHub's own counters in the captured `pull_request` payload agree with the observed per-family counts rather than with the expected figure — review_comments = 3 and comments = 5. UNKNOWN: what became of the two inline records the ground truth implies. No deletion, resolution or hidden-record signal appears in any captured payload, and the archived repository cannot be re-read to establish one.

FACT: both review submissions carry body == "" (an empty string) exactly as returned by the API; no summary text accompanies either submission, and the text of the thread resides in the `review_comments` and `issue_comments` arrays.

FACT: in_reply_to_id is present only on the inline comment that is itself a reply; GitHub omits the field entirely from non-reply inline comments. INFERENCE: its absence on the other inline comments is the API payload shape rather than pruning by this capture; reasoning: the field is absent from the response rather than removed from it, and note[6] records that no record was pruned.

FACT: per-call rate-limit headers are recorded on every entry of `_capture.calls` and are the per-request record; they need not agree with the single snapshot in `_capture.rate_limit_observed`, which was read from the body of GET /rate_limit. As captured: `rate_limit_observed.remaining` = 5000 while the first data call reports `x_ratelimit_remaining` = 4998, a difference of 2, and the reset values differ (1786688475 against 1786688408). INFERENCE: the divergence is expected rather than a defect; reasoning: the ceiling is per credential rather than per process and the token is shared with other sessions in the same window, so any concurrent consumer moves `remaining` between two reads. Both readings are recorded verbatim as observed and neither was adjusted.

FACT: this artifact is raw evidence only. It carries no adjudication of pull request 330, no verdict on its review content and no classification of any kind; that assessment belongs to PROGRAM-PLAN.md Deliverable A #5.

issue_comments.body:
Hi @samdion1994 

Thank you for the tests, it helped tremendously in understanding what is happening.

With that understanding now in place, I cannot approve the pull request, because the expansion of the copybook is no longer happening "in place".
Meaning, we cannot move the working storage elements, to other locations in working storage.
Consider this example:
```
EXEC SQL INCLUDE TEXEM  END-EXEC.
01  TEXEM2 REDEFINES TEXEM.
   10 FULL-NAME PIC X(20).
   10 FILLER PIC X(26).
```
The current changes would move TEXEM below the redefine, meaning the compile would fail.

Looking at the code again, I think the insertion of code is in the correct location, the issue is, that .getFileSectionStatements() is a bad name. Either the function is misused in this context, and there ought to be another function managing the expansion of copybooks, or the function should have another name, making it useable in more contexts.

Cheers, 
Rune

Hi @samdion1994 
Thank you, the new function is a much better encapsulation of what is happening in the code.

But, the changes still moves the expanded copybook to a new location, that will have to be fixed before approval.
Thank you

Cheers

Hi @samdion1994 
Any progress on reverting the changes, that causes the expansion of SQLCA/TEXEM to move from where it was?

Regards 
Rune

Hi rune, Sorry been busy! 

Probably this week :)

Think you can merge this and I could do another fix later?

There a lot of stuff I need to change for this request and little time, but I get what you're saying and I agree that this needs to be fixed. Also I think we might have the same problem with the file section expander.
